newsitem.title: MEXICO: Last Mexican septuplet in grave danger.
newsitem.headline: Last Mexican septuplet in grave danger.

text.p: The sole survivor of Mexico's first birth of septuplets was in grave danger on Tuesday, medical sources said.
A spokesman for the hospital where Fernando Fabian has been in intensive care since his birth on Jan. 21 said he was in a "very serious" state, with lung and brain complications.
The baby weighed just over 2.2 pounds (1 kilogram), he added.
Two of his sisters died over the weekend from a string of problems emanating from the premature multiple birth. Three of the babies died within the first two weeks of birth.

The septuplets, five girls and two boys, were born 12 weeks early during the first pregnancy of their mother, 28-year-old Maria Rocio Diaz. She had taken fertility medicine after trying unsuccessfully to get pregnant for five years.
